title: PR #43 Codex adapter: two decisions under D7
intro: ANSWERED 2026-11-15, applied: D1 accept-both-codex-only; D2 hold-resolve-conflict. The cards show the question as it was asked. See pr43-codex-decisions.md. Original intro: PR #43 adds a Codex worker (phase 2, P2-1) under srt. Two facts were checked by running them. Codex's own sandbox fails inside srt, and Codex needs the trustd Mach grant to reach the gateway. The PR is not merged and conflicts with main in module 09.

decisions.title: Sandbox promise for Codex workers under D7
decisions.ref: D7 worker isolation; module 9 Sandbox; PR #43
decisions.context: Checked on this machine with srt 0.0.83 and codex-cli 0.164.0: Codex with -s workspace-write fails inside srt (sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted), so the adapter uses -s danger-full-access and srt is the only layer. Codex also needs allowMachLookup com.apple.trustd.agent: without it a Codex run through srt timed out (exit 124), with it the run replied ok (exit 0). srt's README says that grant opens a potential data exfiltration route through trustd. The grant is in the Codex settings only; main has none.

options.name: Accept both for Codex workers only, and record them in D7 as residual risk
pros: Both changes are verified to be needed, not optional
Claude workers keep the stricter settings; main has no trustd grant
The risk is written down in D7 where the owner can see it
Reversible: rejecting later only removes the Codex adapter
cons: Codex runs get weaker isolation than Claude runs: one OS layer, and a Mach route srt itself warns about
The exfiltration route is documented by srt but not tested here
D7 now has two isolation levels to keep straight

options.name: Reject both: Codex workers are not allowed in phase 1 or 2 until a stronger sandbox exists
pros: D7 stays exactly as decided: one sandbox level for every worker
cons: P2-1 stays incomplete and Codex cannot be used
Throws away verified work and live smoke runs
No stronger sandbox is planned, so this may be permanent

options.name: Accept the disabled Codex sandbox, but hold the trustd grant until a probe shows what can leave through it
pros: Keeps the unverified route closed until it is measured
Gives a test to cite in D7
cons: Without the grant Codex cannot reach the gateway on macOS, so this is the same as rejecting Codex for now
The probe is new work with no spec behind it
Linux behavior is a separate unknown

decisions.why: Both changes were shown to be required, they apply to Codex only, and writing the residual risk into D7 keeps the decision visible and reversible.

decisions.title: What happens to PR #43 now
decisions.context: PR #43 is open, not merged, and CONFLICTING with main in module 09. Its author reports 749 passed and 2 skipped (not reproduced here) and live Codex and Claude smokes run one at a time. Still open in the PR: the same gate evidence on both harnesses (criterion 20), the doctor canary, the gate-command srt check, cache tests, the api.openai.com default, MCP isolation for Codex, and Linux. Phase 1 rules say phase 2 is not built in phase 1.

options.name: Keep the PR open, have the author resolve the module 09 conflict, and merge only after D1 is recorded in D7
pros: The decision and the merge stay in order
The conflict is small and in one file
Nothing on main changes until D7 says what Codex workers may do
cons: Needs a rebase and a rerun of both suites

options.name: Rebase, rerun both suites, merge now, and open the missing items as tasks
pros: The adapter and the ~/.codex deny-read fix reach main
cons: Merges a weaker isolation level before D7 records it
Criterion 20 and the doctor canary are unproven at merge time
Adds a phase 2 adapter to main during phase 1, as PR #39 and #40 did

options.name: Merge only the ~/.codex deny-read fix now, and hold the rest
pros: The real gap (the gateway key readable under srt) is closed at once
No new isolation level on main
cons: The fix lives in shared sandbox code and the PR author must split it
The adapter work waits for D1

decisions.why: The deny-read fix is valuable and the adapter is not urgent, so the order that keeps D7 honest is decision first, merge second.
